description: Fetch one NWS alert message by ID — a current alert, or an earlier message that an update or cancellation has since superseded and that an active-alert search no longer returns. Takes an id from nws_search_alerts or a references[].identifier from any alert, and returns the same alert fields nws_search_alerts does. The message carries its own references, newest first, so a revision chain is walked one call per message. Every reference sharing the newest sent time is an immediate predecessor (an update can merge several earlier segments), so references[0] is one of them, not always the only one. NWS serves messages for about 7 days after they are sent.

alert_id.description: NWS alert message ID, e.g. "urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.654087301e4bfcbe71d24494c26a965e54d3a1ad.001.1": the id of an alert from nws_search_alerts, or the identifier of one of its references. Pass it exactly as returned; IDs are case-sensitive.

name: nws_get_alert

alert.description: Single alert message with event, severity, area, and timing

affectedZones.description: Affected zones, each with the zone type that decides where it can chain

items.description: Affected zone with its NWS zone type

type.description: NWS zone type: "forecast", "county", or "fire" ("unknown" when upstream reports a shape this server cannot type). A "forecast" code has a zone text forecast: pass it to nws_get_zone_forecast. A "fire" code has a segment in its office's Fire Weather Planning Forecast: call nws_get_office_discussion with office from this alert's office field, product_type "FWF", and sections [code]. All types are valid values for the nws_search_alerts zone filter.

description.description: Full alert description; null when NWS publishes the alert without one

effective.description: Message effective time (ISO 8601) — when this version of the CAP message takes effect. A property of the message, not of the hazard: distinct from onset (when the hazard begins) and from expires (when a superseding message is due). Usually equals sent.

ends.description: Hazard end (ISO 8601) — when the hazard is expected to end; null when open-ended ("until further notice"). Distinct from expires, which is the message-refresh time.

expires.description: Message expiration (ISO 8601) — when NWS will issue a superseding statement. NOT when the hazard ends; the hazard window is described in the headline.

eventMotionDescription.description: Storm time, motion, and position in NWS encoding (e.g., "2026-10-22T17:17:00-00:00...storm...222DEG...11KT...34.0,-118.1")

flashFloodDetection.description: Flash flood detection (e.g., "RADAR INDICATED", "OBSERVED", "RADAR AND GAUGE INDICATED")

hailThreat.description: How the hail is known (e.g., "RADAR INDICATED", "OBSERVED")

maxHailSize.description: Maximum hail size in inches, as NWS states it (e.g., "1.00", "Up to .75")

maxWindGust.description: Maximum wind gust, as NWS states it (e.g., "60 MPH", "34 knots")

windThreat.description: How the wind is known (e.g., "RADAR INDICATED", "OBSERVED")

hazard.description: Severe-weather tags NWS attaches, under NWS key names with values verbatim (free text such as "Up to .75" or "34 knots"). Only the tags NWS sent are present; null when it sent none.

id.description: Alert message ID. Pass it unchanged as alert_id to nws_get_alert to fetch this message again.

messageType.description: CAP message type: "Alert" for an original issuance, "Update" for a revision of an earlier message, "Cancel" for a cancellation.

nwsHeadline.description: The NWS product headline (e.g., "RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON TO 8 PM MDT FRIDAY"), distinct from headline; null when NWS sends none.

office.description: Issuing forecast office code (e.g., "RIW"), from the issuing centre in the message's WMO header; pass it as office to nws_get_office_discussion. Null for tsunami warning centres and national test messages, which have no office discussion, and when NWS sends no usable WMO header.

onset.description: Expected hazard onset (ISO 8601). When the hazard is expected to begin.

references.description: Prior alert messages this one supersedes, newest first by sent instant; messages sent at the same instant keep the order NWS lists them in, and one whose sent time does not parse comes last. Empty for an original issuance — never inferred when NWS reports none. nws_get_alert fetches any of them by identifier. Every reference sharing the newest sent time is an immediate predecessor (an update can merge several earlier segments); the first is one of them.

items.description: One prior message this alert supersedes

identifier.description: CAP identifier of the superseded message. Pass it unchanged as alert_id to nws_get_alert to read that message, which carries its own references.

sent.description: When the superseded message was issued (ISO 8601)

senderName.description: Issuing office name (e.g., "NWS Riverton WY"); the office code nws_get_office_discussion takes is in office

sent.description: Message issuance time (ISO 8601) — when the office transmitted this CAP message. Describes the message, not the hazard: use it to judge how stale the report is.

status.description: This alert's own CAP status as reported by NWS ("Actual", "Exercise", "System", "Test", "Draft"). Distinct from the nws_search_alerts status input filter, which selects which alerts a search covers — with that filter at its default, every alert a search returns reads "Actual".

vtec.description: Raw P-VTEC strings NWS attaches (e.g., "/O.CON.KRIW.FW.W.0031.261023T1800Z-261024T0200Z/"), the key that tracks one event across its updates; empty when NWS sends none (e.g., Special Weather Statements).

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `alert_not_found`: alert_id is not an NWS alert ID, or NWS has no message with that ID. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

title: Nws Get Alert
